Doctor Visit Checklist

A short appointment goes better when you walk in prepared — with your symptoms written down, your medications listed, and the questions you actually want answered. This checklist covers what to bring and note beforehand so nothing important gets forgotten in the moment. It's an organizational aid, not medical advice. Find more health and wellness checklists.

verified Curated by the Gisti team · Updated July 2026

Doctor Visit Checklist · 14 items

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Write down your main reason for the visit and what you hope to resolve

    Leading with your top concern means it gets covered even if the visit runs short.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    List your current symptoms — when each started, how often, and what makes it better or worse
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring an up-to-date list of your medications and doses, including supplements

    Over-the-counter meds and vitamins count; a clear photo of each label works too.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Note any allergies and past reactions to medications
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Write your questions in priority order

    You'll get to the ones that matter even if time runs out.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Pack your insurance card and a photo ID
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Gather recent test results, scans, or reports from other clinics

    Request copies ahead of time if another office is holding them.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Note relevant family medical history, such as heart disease, diabetes, or cancer
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Bring home-tracked numbers if you monitor them — blood pressure, blood sugar, or weight
  • check_box_outline_blank
    List other doctors or specialists you see, and what they treat
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Confirm the date, time, location, and any prep like fasting or forms

    Some blood tests require skipping food that morning — check when you book.

  • check_box_outline_blank
    Have a way to take notes during the visit — a small notepad or your phone
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Arrange for someone to come along if you'd like a second set of ears
  • check_box_outline_blank
    Know which pharmacy you use so any new prescription can be sent there

Frequently asked questions

How do I prepare for a doctor's appointment? expand_more

Write down your symptoms and your questions before you go, and bring a current list of your medications, your allergies, and your insurance and ID. Having it on paper or your phone means you won't forget the one thing you meant to ask when the visit feels rushed.

What should I bring to a doctor visit? expand_more

Bring your insurance card and photo ID, a list of current medications and doses, any recent test results or reports, and your written questions. If you track anything at home — blood pressure, blood sugar, or weight — bring those readings too.

What questions should I ask my doctor? expand_more

Good ones to write down: what the diagnosis means, what your options are, what each medication is for and its side effects, and when to follow up or seek urgent care. This checklist is an organizational aid to help you prepare, not medical advice — your doctor is the person to answer health questions about your situation.
